mark_breakdown.desc: Graph $Y_1 = \cos X$ and $Y_2 = -0.3$ on the same axes
State solutions to the nearest degree: $\theta \approx 107^\circ, 253^\circ$

subparts.solution: We graph the functions $Y_1 = \cos X$ and $Y_2 = -0.3$ on the same set of axes.\\The solutions are $\theta \approx 107^\circ, 253^\circ$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Solving trigonometric equations graphically by finding the intersection points of the function curve and a horizontal line.
step_by_step: Set up a graphing calculator in degree mode.
Plot $Y_1 = \cos X$ and $Y_2 = -0.3$ over the domain $[0^\circ, 360^\circ]$.
Use the intersect feature to find intersection points: $X \approx 107.46^\circ$ and $X \approx 252.54^\circ$.
Round answers to the nearest whole degree: $107^\circ$ and $253^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Reading only one intersection point or having the calculator set to radian mode.
